title: Prefetch Horizon: Batch Weaver and Kernel Adaptor
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Under mixed-production traffic we observe long p99 tail latencies caused by inefficient kernel selection and cold attention state when small prefill bursts hit large-sequence models. Existing admission only gates by queue depth and token budget, but doesn't anticipate upcoming prefill/ decode mixture. Goal: build a prefill-aware admission + batch shaping component (Batch Weaver) that exposes a small horizon window to (1) warm kernel choices and attention paths, (2) shape micro-batches to reduce kernel switching, and (3) smooth tail spikes by crediting token admission. The complementary Kernel Adaptor maps observed sequence-length histograms and attention cache patterns to preferred kernel variants (fp16 / quantized / tiled attention) and memory allocation layouts so we avoid disruptive kernel handoffs during prefills and decodes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) In replayed production traces, p99 end-to-end latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads reduces by >=20% without regressing p50.
2) Kernel switches per request (prefill->decode) reduced by >=40% in median case.
3) No increase in token-level cost >5% for hosted customers.
4) Feature gated and rolloutable per-customer; monitored by new dashboards.
5) All changes behind feature flag 'batch_weaver_v1' with safe default off.
design_notes:
- Prefetch Horizon: maintain a sliding 'horizon' buffer (configurable 50-300ms) that treats incoming prefill tokens as signals to preselect kernel variants and pre-warm attention KV cache allocations.
- Batch Weaver: continuous batch shaper that can micro-slice large batches into kernel-friendly bundles to keep per-kernel occupancy high while honoring latency SLOs. Uses token credit buckets per-tenancy to avoid starving low-priority requests.
- Kernel Adaptor: lightweight runtime that subscribes to recent sequence-length and attention usage histograms and maps to one of a small set of validated kernel recipes. Recipes include parameters: kernel binary id, attention tiling factor, kv-cache-reserve, quantization profile.
- Admission logic: extend current admission controller with two signals: horizon_present (prefill detected) and kernel_affinity_score. Admission decision = base_admission AND (affinity_score > threshold OR horizon_present).
- Fallback: when kernel recipe unavailable or cold, fallback to conservative kernel and mark request for async kernel warmup.
- Telemetry: emit per-request tags (horizon=true/false, recipe_id, kernel_switched) and new metrics (recipe_hit_rate, kernel_switch_count, horizon_latency_delta).
- Configs: horizon_ms, recipe_threshold, micro_slice_target_tokens, per-tenant-credit-rate.
- Safety: fail-open behavior; opt-out via tenant config.
implementation_plan:
1) Spike (2d): implement simulated Prefetch Horizon in replay harness; collect sequence histograms and kernel switch traces.
2) Prototype (5d): implement Batch Weaver with micro-slicing and simple kernel_adaptor using LRU recipe cache. Feature-flagged.
3) Benchmark (3d): run 3 workload classes from production replay: short-chat, long-context, and hybrid prefill-decode bursts. Capture p50/p95/p99, recipe_hit_rate, kernel_switch_count, and token-cost delta.
4) Integrate (3d): wire telemetry and dashboards; add rollout controls per-tenant.
5) Canary (7d): enable for 5% of traffic (low-risk customers) and monitor.
6) Rollout (3-7d): gradual ramp to 50% then 100% contingent on metrics.
7) Postmortem/opt (ongoing): tune recipe mapping thresholds and credit rates.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for admission decision logic, recipe selection, and micro-slicing invariants.
- Integration tests with runtime kernels (mocked) to assert no kernel_switch_count regressions.
- Replay tests with staged traces including synthetic bursts to validate tail smoothing.
- Load test inside dedicated environment with production-like GPUs to validate throughput and token cost.
- Safety regression test: disable feature flag returns to baseline.
monitoring_and_metrics: Emit these new metrics: recipe_hit_rate (per-model, per-tenant), horizon_detection_rate, kernel_switch_count_per_request, p50/p95/p99 with horizon=true/false tags, token_cost_delta_percent. Dashboards: 'Batch Weaver Health' and 'Kernel Adaptor Efficiency'. Alerts: p99 increase >10% sustained for 10m, recipe_hit_rate <70% for a model.
rollout_strategy: Feature-flagged behind 'batch_weaver_v1'. Start internal canary (0.5% synthetic), then production canary (5%), then ramp 25%/50%/100% based on KPIs. Use automated rollback if p99 increases by >10% or token-cost increases >8% for any tenant. Target owners: runtime-team for kernel changes, infra-team for admission controller changes, DX for dashboards.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: mis-mapped recipes cause higher latency. Mitigation: conservative default recipes, staged recipe promotion with A/B tests.
- Risk: increased token cost from micro-slicing inefficiencies. Mitigation: cost cap per-tenant and micro-slice target tuning.
- Risk: overfitting to replay data. Mitigation: include real-time sampling and quick rollbacks.
- Risk: added complexity in admission controller creates deterministic bugs. Mitigation: small, audited changes and feature gating.
notes: Related research: attention-tiling reduced kernel memory churn in internal perf paper (2025-Q3). Aligns with ongoing Kernel Profiling effort (ENG-333210). This ticket focuses on tying kernel-choice to short-term prefill signals rather than longer-term model-level heuristics.
